# Viz Factory Component Gallery (With Examples)

The `VizFactory (viz_factory.py)` translates simple YAML configurations into highly complex Plotnine (`ggplot2`) graphical objects. This appendix provides concrete "copy-paste" examples for non-programmers to define their own visual aesthetics without touching Python code.

> **Blueprint Architect IDE**: Plot components annotated with `ui_schema` are discoverable via the component picker (see §0). The schema drives automatic form generation — labels, widget types, and validation rules are declared once in the decorator.

## 0. Blueprint IDE Component Catalog (ADR-075) {#sec-ui-schema}

### What is a component `ui_schema`?

Every `@register_plot_component` decorator in the viz_factory can carry a `ui_schema` dict. When present, the component appears in the Blueprint Architect IDE's component picker with an auto-generated form. The schema describes which plotnine parameters to expose, what widget to use for each, and how the component maps back to the underlying plotnine function.

### Accessing the catalog programmatically

```python
import viz_factory   # triggers all @register_plot_component decorators

from blueprint_arch.schema_registry import (
    get_component_catalog,         # all annotated components
    get_components_for_context,    # filter by "plot"
)

# All annotated plot components
catalog = get_component_catalog()

# Same — all geoms/stats/themes/scales are "plot" context
plot_comps = get_components_for_context("plot")
```

### Schema field reference

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | Yes | Human-readable name shown in the IDE picker |
| `category` | Yes | Visualization family (see vocabulary below) |
| `context` | Yes | Always `["plot"]` for geom/stat/theme/scale components |
| `tags` | Yes | Search keywords for the picker |
| `wraps` | Yes | Link to plotnine source (`lib`, `attr_path`) |
| `allow_extra_params` | Yes | Must be `True` — allows any valid plotnine kwarg via data analysis recipe |
| `params` | Yes | Dict of param definitions (widget, label, required, …) |

### Category vocabulary

| Category | Visual purpose |
|---|---|
| `distribution` | Show spread, quartiles, density — boxplot, violin, histogram |
| `correlation` | Show relationships between variables — scatter, bubble |
| `comparison` | Compare values across groups — bar, column, lollipop |
| `evolution` | Show change over time — line, area, step |
| `part-to-whole` | Show proportions — stacked bar, pie equivalent |
| `ranking` | Order items by value — sorted bar, dot plot |
| `annotation` | Add context to a plot — labels, reference lines, text |
| `uncertainty` | Show confidence, error, range — errorbar, ribbon |

### Annotated components (BP-SCHEMA-1)

Virtually every registered plot component carries a `ui_schema` dict and appears in the Blueprint IDE
picker — 191 components registered (`grep -c '^@register_plot_component(' libs/viz_factory/src/viz_factory/**/*.py`),
essentially all of them annotated (`grep -rc ui_schema` on the same files returns almost exactly one
hit per component, give or take a docstring mention). A handful of frequently-used examples:

| Component | Category | Core params |
|---|---|---|
| `geom_boxplot` | `distribution` | alpha, fill, colour, size, width, notch, linetype, position, stat, outlier_colour/shape/size |
| `geom_point` | `correlation` | alpha, colour, fill, size, shape, stroke, na_rm |
| `geom_line` | `evolution` | alpha, colour, size, linetype, lineend, linejoin, na_rm |
| `geom_bar` | `comparison` | alpha, fill, colour, size, stat (count/identity), position (stack/dodge/fill), width |
| `geom_histogram` | `distribution` | alpha, fill, colour, bins, binwidth, stat, position |
| `geom_tile` | `correlation` | alpha, fill, colour, width, height, linejoin |
| `labs` | `annotation` | title, subtitle, caption, x, y, fill, colour, size, shape, alpha |

The count will drift as the registry grows (ADR-035/036 parity mandate) — treat the number above as
"essentially all of them," not a fixed total, and re-run the `grep` above if you need the exact figure.
The `ui_schema` only controls IDE discoverability; every registered component, annotated or not, works
from YAML data analysis recipes.

### Why `allow_extra_params: True`?

Components do `p + geom_bar(**spec)` — the spec dict passes through directly to plotnine. The `params` dict lists the most common kwargs for the form renderer, but any valid plotnine kwarg can be added directly in the data analysis recipe YAML. Setting `allow_extra_params: True` tells the form renderer to allow this without validation errors.

### Adding a `ui_schema` to a new component (developer guide)

```python
from viz_factory.registry import register_plot_component

@register_plot_component("geom_mygeom", ui_schema={
    "label": "My Geom",
    "category": "distribution",           # use the semantic vocabulary above
    "context": ["plot"],                   # always ["plot"] for geoms
    "tags": ["distribution", "my-geom"],
    "wraps": [{"lib": "plotnine", "attr_path": ["geom_mygeom"]}],
    "allow_extra_params": True,
    "params": {
        "alpha": {
            "widget": "number",
            "label": "Opacity (0–1)",
            "required": False,
            "default": 1.0,
        },
        "fill": {
            "widget": "color",
            "label": "Fill colour (fixed, not mapped)",
            "required": False,
        },
    },
})
def handle_mygeom(p, spec):
    from plotnine import geom_mygeom
    return p + geom_mygeom(**spec)
```

**Rules:**
- `wraps[0].attr_path` must contain the component name exactly as registered.
- Every geom should expose `alpha` — it is checked by `test_component_schemas.py::test_all_geoms_have_alpha`.
- Verify registration with `libs/viz_factory/tests/test_component_schemas.py`.

## 1. Anatomy of a Plot Data Analysis Recipe

Every plot spec in the dashboard follows this exact skeleton (ADR-083 grammar-of-graphics format;
canonical reference: `.claude/rules/rules_data_analysis_recipe_structure.md §8`). Aesthetics live under
`mapping:`; visual layers live in an ordered `layers:` list, each a `{name, params}` pair:

```yaml
spec:
  target_dataset: AMR_Profile_Joint
  mapping:
    x: collection_year
    y: resistance_score
    color: species
  layers:
    - name: geom_point
      params:
        alpha: 0.7
    - name: theme_minimal
      params: {}
```

The `layers` list acts as a painter's canvas. Layers are painted exactly in the order they are listed.
`VizFactory.render()` reads each entry's `name` key to look up the registered component — it has never
read a `components:` list or a `type:` key (see `libs/viz_factory/src/viz_factory/viz_factory.py`,
`layer_spec.get("name")`). The old `components: [{type: "geom_point", ...}]` / flat-kwargs shape shown
in earlier revisions of this file is **not** read by the engine; a data analysis recipe written that
way renders nothing for those layers, with no error.

---

## 2. Geometries (Data Shapes)

Every example below is a single entry in a plot spec's `layers:` list (see §1 for the full skeleton).

### `geom_point` (Scatter Plot)
Used for creating scatter plots mapping X and Y coordinates.
```yaml
- name: geom_point
  params:
    size: 3
    alpha: 0.6
    shape: "o"
```

### `geom_bar` (Bar Charts)
Used for counting occurrences or plotting raw values.
```yaml
- name: geom_bar
  params:
    stat: "identity"  # Use "identity" if your Y-value is already calculated
    position: "dodge" # Use "dodge" to place bars side-by-side, or "stack"
    alpha: 0.8
```

### `geom_boxplot` (Distributions)
Visualizes data quartiles and outliers.
```yaml
- name: geom_boxplot
  params:
    fill: "#E0E0E0"
    outlier_colour: "red"
    outlier_size: 2
```

### `geom_smooth` (Trend Lines / Regressions)
Adds an automatic trendline with an optional confidence ribbon.
```yaml
- name: geom_smooth
  params:
    method: "lm"      # Linear model
    se: true          # Show confidence interval
    colour: "black"
    linetype: "dashed"
```

### `geom_text` (Labels)
Draws text directly onto the plot coordinates. Make sure `label` is defined in the main `mapping`.
```yaml
- name: geom_text
  params:
    size: 10
    nudge_y: 0.5      # Push the text slightly above the point
    check_overlap: true
```

### `geom_density_2d` (2D Density)
Visualizes the density of a 2D distribution with contours.
```yaml
- name: geom_density_2d
  params:
    colour: "blue"
```

### `geom_pointdensity` (Density-Colored Scatter)
Colors points by local density.
```yaml
- name: geom_pointdensity
  params: {}
```

### `geom_sina` (Sina Plot)
A combination of a violin plot and jittered points.
```yaml
- name: geom_sina
  params:
    alpha: 0.5
```

### Reference Lines (`geom_hline`, `geom_vline`, `geom_abline`)
Used to add static reference boundaries or diagonal thresholds.
```yaml
layers:
  - name: geom_hline     # Horizontal
    params:
      yintercept: 10
      colour: "red"
  - name: geom_vline     # Vertical
    params:
      xintercept: 5
      linetype: "dashed"
  - name: geom_abline    # Slope/Intercept
    params:
      slope: 1
      intercept: 0
```

### `geom_errorbar` (Uncertainty)
Draws vertical error bars for confidence intervals.
```yaml
- name: geom_errorbar
  params:
    width: 0.2
```

### `geom_segment` (Lollipops / Connections)
Draws straight lines between points. Requires `xend` and `yend` in mapping.
```yaml
- name: geom_segment
  params:
    alpha: 0.5
```

## 3. Advanced Enclosures & Statistics

### `stat_ellipse` (Clustering)
Calculates and draws a multivariate normal confidence ellipse.
```yaml
- name: stat_ellipse
  params:
    level: 0.95
    geom: "polygon"
    alpha: 0.2
```

### `stat_hull` (Convex Hull)
Draws a boundary around the outermost points of a group. Great for PCA/UMAP clusters.
```yaml
- name: stat_hull
  params:
    fill: "lightblue"
    alpha: 0.3
```

### `stat_summary` (Aggregations)
Automatically calculates and plots mean, median, or custom summaries without pre-wrangling.
```yaml
- name: stat_summary
  params:
    fun_data: "mean_cl_boot" # 95% Confidence Interval
    geom: "errorbar"
    width: 0.1
```

---

## 4. Scales (Colors & Axes)

Scales translate your raw data categories into physical attributes like hex colors or axis limits.

### `scale_color_manual` (Custom Target Colors)
Forces specific colors onto specific categories.
```yaml
- name: scale_color_manual
  params:
    values:
      "E. coli": "#E41A1C"
      "Salmonella": "#377EB8"
```

### `scale_fill_viridis_d` (Colorblind Safe Palettes)
Automatically applies the highly readable Viridis palette to categorical fills.
```yaml
- name: scale_fill_viridis_d
  params:
    option: "plasma"  # Options: magma, inferno, plasma, viridis
    alpha: 0.9
```

### `scale_x_continuous` (Numeric Axis Controls)
Used to format quantitative axes.
```yaml
- name: scale_x_continuous
  params:
    limits: [1990, 2025]
    breaks: [1990, 2000, 2010, 2020]
```

### `scale_y_log10` (Logarithmic Transformation)
Transforms the axis scaling mathematically without needing to mutate the raw dataframe.
```yaml
- name: scale_y_log10
  params: {}
```

### `scale_x_sqrt` (Square Root)
Compresses large spreads in quantitative data.
```yaml
- name: scale_x_sqrt
  params: {}
```

### `scale_x_symlog` (Symmetric Log)
Handles both positive and negative values on a logarithmic scale.
```yaml
- name: scale_x_symlog
  params: {}
```

### `scale_x_date` (Timeline Control)
Formatting for date-based axes.
```yaml
- name: scale_x_date
  params:
    date_labels: "%b %Y"
    date_breaks: "6 months"
```

### `scale_stroke_continuous` (Outline Scaling)
Dynamically size the outlines of shapes based on quantitative data.
```yaml
- name: scale_stroke_continuous
  params:
    range: [1, 5]
```

## 5. Facets (Multi-Panel Splitters)

Facets split a single large dataset into a grid of smaller, identical plots based on a column variable.
(A single grouping variable can also be set directly via `mapping: {facet_by: <column>}` — see
`rules_data_analysis_recipe_structure.md §8` — which is equivalent to a `facet_wrap` layer.)

### `facet_wrap`
Wraps panels sequentially like reading a book. Best for 1 variable.
```yaml
- name: facet_wrap
  params:
    facets: species
    ncol: 3
    scales: "free_y" # Allows each subplot to have its own dynamic Y-axis
```

### `facet_grid`
Creates a strict 2D matrix of plots. Best for crossing 2 variables.
```yaml
- name: facet_grid
  params:
    rows: source_type
    cols: species
```

## 6. Themes & Aesthetics

Themes control the non-data ink (backgrounds, gridlines, fonts, legend positions).

### `theme_minimal`
Removes the grey background and cleans up heavy gridlines.
```yaml
- name: theme_minimal
  params: {}
```

### `theme_bw`
Classic scientific black-and-white framing.
```yaml
- name: theme_bw
  params: {}
```

### `theme_seaborn` (Statistical Aesthetic)
Mimics the default styling of the Python Seaborn library.
```yaml
- name: theme_seaborn
  params: {}
```

### `theme_538` (Data Journalism Style)
Inspired by FiveThirtyEight's distinct data visualizations.
```yaml
- name: theme_538
  params: {}
```

### `theme_xkcd` (Hand-Drawn Style)
For "sketch" style plots (uses internal font mapping).
```yaml
- name: theme_xkcd
  params: {}
```

### `theme_tufte` (Minimalist)
Based on Edward Tufte's principles of maximizing data-ink ratio.
```yaml
- name: theme_tufte
  params: {}
```

### Legend Management (via `theme_custom`)
`theme_custom` is the registered "arbitrary theme override" component — there is no generic
`type: "theme"` component in the registry. Use it to pass any plotnine `theme()` kwarg directly, or
nest an `element_text`/`element_line`/`element_rect`/`element_blank` block for a specific element:
```yaml
- name: theme_custom
  params:
    legend_position: "bottom"
    legend_title: {name: element_blank}     # Hides the legend title
    axis_text_x:
      name: element_text
      params:
        angle: 45               # Rotates bottom text for easy reading
        hjust: 1
```
For a single named axis/strip text tweak, `element_text` can also be used directly as its own layer
(see `libs/viz_factory/src/viz_factory/themes/core.py`):
```yaml
- name: element_text
  params:
    target: axis_text_x
    angle: 45
    hjust: 1
```
And for the common case of only moving the legend, `theme_legend_position` is a lighter-weight
dedicated component:
```yaml
- name: theme_legend_position
  params:
    position: bottom
```

## 7. Gallery Taxonomy (6-Axis Classification)

Every example in the Viz Gallery is tagged across **six axes** that drive the sidebar filter panels in the Gallery tab. Authors must populate all six fields in the `info` block of their `data_analysis_recipe.yaml` before a submission is accepted.

### Icon → Axis reference

| Icon | Axis | Data analysis recipe key | Sidebar label |
|------|------|-------------|--------------|
| 📊 | **Family (Purpose)** | `info.family` | `📊 Family (Purpose)` |
| 🔢 | **Data Pattern** | `info.pattern` | `🔢 Data Pattern` |
| 📈 | **Difficulty** | `info.difficulty` | `📈 Difficulty` |
| ⚙️ | **Primary Geom** | `info.geom` | `⚙️ Primary Geom` |
| 🎯 | **What it Shows** | `info.show` | `🎯 What it Shows` |
| 📏 | **Sample Size** | `info.sample_size` | `📏 Sample Size` |

### Allowed values

**📊 Family (Purpose):** `Comparison` · `Correlation` · `Distribution` · `Evolution` · `Part-to-Whole` · `Ranking`

**🔢 Data Pattern:** `1 Numeric` · `1 Numeric, 1 Categorical` · `1 Numeric, 2 Categorical` · `1 Numeric, 2 Categorical (Faceted)` · `2 Numeric` · `2 Numeric, 1 Categorical` · `2 Numeric, 1 Categorical (Faceted)` · `3 Numeric (Matrix)` · `1 Year, 1 Numeric` · `1 Year, 1 Numeric, 1 Categorical`

**📈 Difficulty:** `Simple` · `Intermediate` · `Advanced`

**⚙️ Primary Geom:** the first `geom_*` or `stat_*` layer — use the exact plotnine function name, e.g. `geom_histogram`, `geom_violin`, `geom_point` (see §2 for the full list of supported geometries).

**🎯 What it Shows:** `change` · `distribution` · `frequency` · `normality` · `proportion` · `ranking` · `relationship` · `trend` · `uncertainty`

**📏 Sample Size:** `any` · `individual points` · `medium+` · `large`

### Data analysis recipe `info` block

```yaml
info:
  name: Step list Name
  submission_date: 'YYYY-MM-DD'
  family: Distribution              # 📊
  pattern: 1 Numeric, 1 Categorical # 🔢
  difficulty: Intermediate          # 📈
  geom: geom_violin                 # ⚙️
  show: distribution                # 🎯
  sample_size: medium+              # 📏
```

### `example_meta.md` tag strip

Every `example_meta.md` must include a blockquote tag strip on line 3 (immediately after the `## Steps Name` heading and a blank line):

```markdown
## Violin + Boxplot Overlay

> 📊 Distribution · 🔢 1 Numeric, 1 Categorical · 📈 Intermediate · ⚙️ geom_violin · 🎯 distribution · 📏 medium+
```
